subject: Request: Availability floor adjustment for burst-heavy workload
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Availability floor ask for burst-heavy workloads

Hi Soojin / Laura —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. We ran an internal ops review and wanted to surface a request related to the SLA floor for a subset of our traffic. Nimbus has a class of short, bursty inference jobs (billing & fraud checks) that spike unpredictably but are low overall monthly token volume. For those jobs we need a realistic availability target that reflects the burst risk profile; our security and procurement teams are asking if Redwood will accept a temporary floor of 99.60% (vs. the standard 99.95%) for these named workloads, in exchange for a capped monthly credit mechanism.

Specifically: can Redwood:
- Agree to 99.60% uptime for workload group "Nimbus-burst" (definition attached),
- Limit monthly service credits for that group to a fixed pool equal to 5% of our subscription fee for the affected services, and
- Add an audit/usage attachment (we've included a CSV) to help baseline the monthly exposure?

We'd appreciate a proposed amendment we can share with Legal.

Attachments: burst-patterns-usage-jun-may.csv

Best,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Operations
Nimbus Analytics

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability floor ask for burst-heavy workloads

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the clear ask and for the usage CSV. We want to be pragmatic here — our standard hosted SLA is 99.95% availability but we understand that some bursty workloads have asymmetric risk. A few clarifying questions from our side before we draft an amendment:

1) Is "Nimbus-burst" going to be routed to the Hosted API or to a Dedicated pool? That affects our mitigation options.
2) Do you expect the burst group to be >5% of your monthly requests in peak months? (CSV suggests small but occasional spikes).
3) For the credit cap: would Nimbus accept a fixed-dollar monthly cap (e.g., equivalent to 5% of your current monthly invoice) instead of a percentage-based credit?

Operationally we can propose two paths:
A) Hosted amendment: 99.60% for named workload with a fixed monthly credit cap and a requirement to use our suggested batching/caching profile to mitigate noise.
B) Dedicated carve-out: keep 99.95% but run the bursters on a Dedicated pool with pre-warmed capacity (higher monthly commitment).

I'll loop in Legal to get a draft amendment for path A if that's the direction you prefer. Open to a short call this week to finalize scoping.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability floor ask for burst-heavy workloads

Looping in a draft term we can consider (high-level):

- Scoped workload: "Nimbus-burst" (exact endpoints + prefix list to be attached)
- Availability floor: 99.60% measured per calendar month for the scoped workload only
- Monthly credit mechanism: fixed-dollar pool equal to $X (we'll compute X = 5% of current monthly invoice; Samira please confirm current MRR for these services)
- Observability: Redwood will publish token-level uptime for the scoped workload to a mutually accessible dashboard; both parties agree to a 14-day dispute window for incidents impacting reported availability
- Exclusions: planned maintenance (48-hour rolling window notification) and region-wide cloud provider incidents will be excluded per standard carveouts

If Nimbus wants an alternative to credits, we can talk about a remediation pool (one-time engineering allocation for faster recovery) but that would require SRE scheduling commitments and is usually part of a Dedicated agreement.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Nimbus Legal <legal@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 10:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Availability floor ask for burst-heavy workloads

Thanks — Legal has a couple of standard asks before we can sign an amendment:

1) Definition clarity: the exact hostnames/endpoint prefixes for "Nimbus-burst" must be enumerated or referenced to an agreed tag.
2) Credit calculation: credits must be applied pro rata to affected invoices and limited in aggregate per 12-month period (we'd prefer a 12-month cap vs monthly).
3) Remedy lag: require that credits be issued within 30 days of validated incident determination.

We prefer a 12-month aggregate cap of 60% of one month (effectively the monthly 5% private cap multiplied), but can be flexible if Redwood provides better outage reporting and a shorter dispute resolution SLA.

Please provide the draft amendment and a short example showing how credits would apply for a sample outage.

Regards,
Evan Park
Senior Counsel, Nimbus Analytics

Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability floor ask for burst-heavy workloads

Samira / Evan —

Appreciate the quick review. Proposed compromise from Redwood:

1) Scoped amendment will name endpoints and a tag-based rule set for "Nimbus-burst."
2) Availability floor: 99.60% measured per calendar month for named workload when routed to Hosted API.
3) Monthly credit: fixed-dollar pool equal to 5% of Nimbus's then-current monthly bill for the affected service; credits are applied to the next invoice and may not exceed an aggregate 12-month cap equal to 60% of one month’s bill (i.e., 12 x monthly caps cannot be exceeded).
4) Credits will be issued within 30 days of validated incident conclusion and after the 14-day dispute window.
5) Exclusions: planned maintenance (with 48-hour notification) and major cloud provider outages.

We will attach an example calculation to the draft amendment and share a clean PDF (attached). If this aligns, we can do a short approval call Monday and get Legal signatures the same week.

Attachments: nimbus-sla-amend-draft.pdf (clean), example-credit-calculation.xlsx

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
